clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's stroke in June 1991: within months your wrist injury stopped your playing, you and your roommate Rafe clashed and he moved out, you were on your own getting high and absorbed in fixing radios, then lost and low unable to get going with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry. Your closest friend's move that autumn and your mother filling in your college forms sit beside these shifts. By early 1994, an exchange in Portugal and your drive returning, things settled; your cousin Bella's melanoma treatment that year is left out, since no shift in your own family's ties around it shows then.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother's cancer found in 2001 or 2002: within months you ran out of steam for performing, had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra and were done with it, you were on poor terms with family and friends and left Thornbury for Gull Harbour. You met Marisol at a winter party, moved to Fenwick to live with her, then within the year split up and sank into a deep depression. You could not face your parents, but relied on friends; your father spoke with Corbin during your stay. By early 2004 you returned to your therapist, your functioning began coming back, and your grandmother died in February; the brief visit you made to her sickroom before the airport, hung over and cutting it short, falls in these months but marks your distance then, not a shift away from it.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2009
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008: within months you were at Alder Creek building with Silas and too drained for conversation with your mother, she pressed you to visit and you kept the door shut on her, then when you left for nursing school in August you stopped speaking to her, a silence that held roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke in January 2009 with months of rehabilitation ahead. By late 2008 the cutoff was set; the quiet that followed held through your first year at school.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017: within months you saw your mother a bit less, your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, your sister Tara married James and began flying for a regional airline, her baby was on the way by October 2019. In October 2019 your partner was swamped with a street party, a fundraising dinner and her mother's retirement, you were overfunctioning laying out a plan to settle her, she is fused with her father and brother talking all day, at the lake weekend you were awake from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as others rose, feeling you don't belong, and your partner grew anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions. By late 2019 these shifts were piling up around you both; your job had steadied and paid well, but you constantly felt you ought to be driving your projects forward and started a sleeping pill, and you aimed for shorter regular calls with your mother to soften the distance that piles up. Your aunt Imogen had memory lapses worsening since 2015, lashes out when muddled, and Hal has been driving her to the coast for care.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
